\section[tandem]{tandem — at last}

\label{lesson:LA-C175-tandem}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for a voice, then the Latin for mind.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: tandem}
\textbf{tandem} — \textquotedblleft{}at last\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{tandem} is \emph{tam}, \textquotedblleft{}so far\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-dem}, a pointing ending (Lewis \& Short): so far and no further, at last.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}

\textbf{adhūc} — \textquotedblleft{}still, until now\textquotedblright{}.

\section[subitō]{subitō — suddenly}

\label{lesson:LA-C175-subito}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for from now on, then the Latin for still.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: subitō}
\textbf{subitō} — \textquotedblleft{}suddenly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{subitō} comes from the participle of \emph{subeō}, \textquotedblleft{}to come up from under\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), \emph{subitus}, \textquotedblleft{}sudden\textquotedblright{}: coming up unseen.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[dōnec]{dōnec — until; while}

\label{lesson:LA-C175-donec}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for still, then the Latin for suddenly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: dōnec}
\textbf{dōnec} — \textquotedblleft{}until; while\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{dōnec} comes from older \emph{dōnicum} (Lewis \& Short), but how that was formed is uncertain; Lewis \& Short suggest an old word for \textquotedblleft{}day\textquotedblright{} with \emph{cum}, \textquotedblleft{}when\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
